author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell revisited his long standing discomfort with the Five Eyes intelligence alliance, a system originally built to let countries like Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and the US spy on each other's citizens as a workaround to their own domestic surveillance laws. He admitted he'd always found the name almost friendly sounding, joking it reminded him of Five Guys burgers rather than anything sinister. Russell reacted with genuine unease to the idea of a sixth eye potentially joining that system, given the vast intelligence and military technology already being shared among the existing members. Some expansions sound harmless until you actually think about what they're expanding.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reflected on the World Cup as a rare source of unity in a deeply politicized and fractured world, describing sport as a kind of sanitized war that still manages to bring people together across cultures. He talked about football functioning almost like a universal language, where mentioning a single player's name instantly connects strangers anywhere in the world. Russell also pointed out how World Cups mark time in a strange, personal way, with entire lives measured out in four year intervals between tournaments. Even so, he reminded himself that everything the world offers, however unifying it feels, still pales next to what truly matters.
